title: Cryptography Engineer Roadmap
summary: A four-year engineering path focused on mathematics, algorithms, number theory, cryptographic protocols, secure systems, programming, applied cryptography and post-quantum cryptography.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a four-year B.Tech/B.E. programme beginning in 2026 and graduating around 2030.

about.label: Career-route check
about.text: Cryptography Engineer is a specialised cybersecurity career. A CSE - Cyber Security degree provides a suitable foundation, but advanced cryptography roles often require substantially stronger mathematics and, for research-heavy positions, postgraduate study.

blocks.text: Use the additional honours year for advanced algebra/number theory, cryptographic protocol research, formal methods, hardware security or an extended research internship.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Develop from implementing cryptographic primitives toward designing and reviewing secure protocols, key-management systems and cryptographic architectures. Maintain awareness of post-quantum standards, implementation vulnerabilities and formal verification.

Progression varies substantially. Research-heavy cryptography positions may require a master's or PhD, while applied cryptographic engineering positions can be reached through strong software and security engineering experience.
PhD routes

Develop expertise in cryptographic protocol design, secure implementation, formal verification, key management and post-quantum migration. At senior levels, the role increasingly involves reviewing security assumptions and architectures rather than simply implementing individual algorithms.
